research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and OSR sources only; outcome 14-22 definitions, CSEW response/reporting and weighting, police-recorded revision/QA, comparability and governance controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSEW fraud full-sample coverage
verified_claims: fraud and computer-misuse questions initially went to half the sample
from October 2017 they were asked of the full sample
the staged design protected the historical survey series while testing burden
limitations: half-sample and full-sample periods need design metadata
sample expansion is not an incident-date change

sources.name: CSEW social-desirability error
verified_claims: some respondents may say they reported a crime to police when they did not
ONS identifies this as a socially desirable response risk
the issue is a non-sampling error
limitations: self-reported police contact is not administrative proof
the direction and size of bias may vary

sources.name: CSEW interviewer and coder error
verified_claims: some incidents can be miscoded during interview or coding
specially trained coders assign offence codes
coding quality is a separate uncertainty source from sampling error
limitations: a coded survey offence is not a police-recorded offence
miscoding risk must not be ignored in small differences

sources.name: Live police administrative system
verified_claims: police recorded crime is produced from a live administrative system
records can change as investigations proceed
offence categories can change, for example from theft to robbery
limitations: published snapshots are not immutable event logs
later classifications can supersede earlier ones

sources.name: Monthly provisional police returns
verified_claims: forces send provisional figures to the Home Office monthly
returns include revised totals for previously supplied months
Home Office validation can prompt resubmission
limitations: monthly values must be versioned
a revised month must not be counted as an additional month

sources.name: Eight-quarter police QA snapshot
verified_claims: every three months the Home Office takes a database snapshot
forces receive counts for the last eight quarters to quality assure
historical counts can be updated during this process
limitations: snapshot QA does not create an immutable historical series
the snapshot date must accompany extracted values

sources.name: Current-versus-prior release revisions
verified_claims: figures for the same period may differ between publications
differences reflect subsequent force revisions
ONS states revisions tend to be small
limitations: small revisions are not zero revisions
values must be tied to publication edition

sources.name: Quarterly revision-difference table
verified_claims: quarterly data tables include differences between current and preceding publications
the table supports revision transparency
revisions are part of the official release process
limitations: a difference table is not a replacement for the current data table
revision direction must not be inferred without values

sources.name: Crime release timeliness
verified_claims: Crime in England and Wales is published quarterly
publication is approximately 14 weeks after quarter end
timeliness is distinct from punctuality
limitations: the lag is approximate rather than guaranteed
publication lag is not incident-to-police lag

sources.name: Police-recorded pre-2003 comparability boundary
verified_claims: HOCR and NCRS implementation prevents direct comparison of police recorded crime before YE March 2003
the boundary affects long-term police series
HMICFRS inspections provide force-variation context
limitations: pre-2003 figures are not invalid but require separate methodology
the boundary does not apply identically to CSEW
